'''Stanislav Gennadyevich Galaktionov''' ({{lang|ru|Станисла́в Генна́дьевич Галактио́нов}}; 7 March 1937 – 8 April 2011) was a Soviet and American biologist. Born into a family of engineers, he pursued a scientific career in the Soviet Union before emigrating to the United States in 1991. He died in 2011.

Galaktionov graduated from the [[Belarusian State Technological University|Belarusian Forestry Institute]] and worked at the Institute of Biology of the [[Belarusian Academy of Sciences]]. He held research posts in [[Minsk]] (at the {{ill|A. V. Lykov Institute of Heat and Mass Transfer|lt=Institute of Heat and Mass Transfer|ru|Институт тепло- и массообмена имени А. В. Лыкова НАН Беларуси}} and the {{ill|State Research Institute for Genetics and Selection of Industrial Microorganisms|lt=All-Union Research Institute for Genetics and Selection of Industrial Microorganisms|ru|ГосНИИгенетика}}), in [[Riga]] (at the {{ill|Latvian Institute of Organic Synthesis|lt=Latvian Institute of Organic Synthesis|ru|Институт органического синтеза Академии наук Латвии}}), and in [[St. Louis]] (at [[Washington University in St. Louis|Washington University]]).

He was among the early researchers in [[molecular modelling]], specializing in [[peptides]] and [[proteins]] with applications in [[medicinal chemistry]] and [[drug design]]. He developed computational approaches for [[Conformational analysis|analyzing conformations]], [[structure–activity relationship]]s, and receptor interactions of biologically active peptides and proteins, and worked on the design of [[peptide drugs]] with enhanced stability and efficacy. By 1988, Galaktionov had published over 100 scientific works and several popular science books, some of which remained in use in university curricula in [[Russia]], [[Belarus]] and [[Ukraine]] through at least 2016.

Galaktionov’s work was noted as enhancing the prestige of the Belarusian {{ill|Institute of Experimental Botany|lt=Institute of Experimental Botany|ru|Институт экспериментальной ботаники имени В. Ф. Купревича НАН Беларуси}}. He was recognized by Soviet, Belarusian and American scientists for his research on peptide structure and [[protein fold]] prediction and important contributions to [[molecular modelling]]. His work was later praised by Western colleagues such as [[Harold Scheraga]] and {{ill|Garland R. Marshall|de|Garland R. Marshall}}. Galaktionov was known for his support of the research work of his colleagues.

== Biography ==
Stanislav Galaktionov was born on 7 March 1937 in [[Smolensk]], [[Soviet Union]].<ref>{{Cite web |language=en |url=http://www.tributes.com/show/Stan-Galaktionov-91319597 |title=Stan Galaktionov Obituary – Mobile, Alabama |publisher=Tributes.com |access-date=29 April 2012 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304075353/http://www.tributes.com/show/Stan-Galaktionov-91319597 |url-status=live}}</ref> His parents worked at the Smolensk Machine-Building Plant, where his mother later became chief engineer.<ref name="marina">Marina G. Galaktionova, "My Older Brother: Childhood and Youth", in: ''Amazing Human Being'', pp. 124–129.</ref> After the death of his father in 1951, the family moved to [[Minsk]], where his mother became chief engineer at the {{ill|Amkodor|lt=Udarnik Plant|ru|Амкодор}}.<ref name="DNDW5-8">''Dokhodyaga News and Daily Woply'', Vol. 5, no. 8, 31 May 1997.</ref>

He graduated from the [[Belarusian State Technological University|Belarusian Forestry Institute]], held research posts in Minsk and Riga, and defended his Candidate (1963)<ref name="nan" /><ref name=":0" /> and Doctor of Biological Sciences (1973)<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /> dissertations. In 1991, he emigrated to the United States,<ref name="pavel115" /> and was granted American citizenship in 1996.<ref name="DNDW5-3">''Dokhodyaga News and Daily Woply'', Vol. 5, no. 3, 31 December 1996.</ref>

In July 2001, Galaktionov suffered a severe [[traumatic brain injury]], which ended his scientific career. In 2002, he moved to [[Mobile, Alabama]], where his daughter lived with her family.<ref name="slovo" /><ref name="lora">Leonora M. Mikhnova, "About My Husband", in: ''Amazing Human Being'', pp. 142–147.</ref> He died on 8 April 2011 following complications after heart surgery<ref>Leonora M. Mikhnova, "About My Husband", in: ''Amazing Human Being'', p. 153.</ref> and was buried at the [[Mobile Botanical Gardens]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Uskow |first=Yuras |date=20 April 2011 |title=Бацька малекулярнага мадэлявання. У ЗША памёр беларускі навуковец Станіслаў Галакціёнаў|trans-title=Father of molecular modeling. Belarusian scientist Stanislav Galaktionov dies in the US |url=https://nashaniva.com/53547 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813171349/https://nashaniva.com/?c=ar&i=53547 |archive-date=13 August 2022 |access-date=8 August 2025 |website=[[Nasha Niva]] |publisher=Surodzichy Publishing |language=be}}</ref>

== Career ==
After graduating, Galaktionov took a position as a senior laboratory assistant at the Institute of Biology of the [[Belarusian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="marina" />

In January 1960, Galaktionov was admitted to the postgraduate program at the {{ill|Institute of Experimental Botany|lt=Institute of Experimental Botany|ru|Институт экспериментальной ботаники имени В. Ф. Купревича НАН Беларуси}}. In 1963, at the age of 27, he defended his Candidate of Biological Sciences dissertation on the effect of [[chloride]] ions in [[potash fertilizer]]s on potato yields.<ref name="nan" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |url=http://dep.nlb.by/jspui/handle/nlb/39346 |title=On the Nature of the Toxic Effect of Chlorides on Potatoes |date=1963 |publisher=[[National Library of Belarus]] |access-date=10 September 2023}}</ref> At the same time, he attended an extensive series of courses at the Faculty of Physics of [[Belarusian State University]], adding to his general biological erudition a perspective on biological processes from the standpoint of [[physics]], as well as knowledge of [[Mathematics|mathematical]] methods.{{sfn|Nikiforovich|2012|p=445}}

In 1967, he joined the {{ill|A. V. Lykov Institute of Heat and Mass Transfer|lt=Institute of Heat and Mass Transfer of the Belarusian Academy of Sciences|ru|Институт тепло- и массообмена имени А. В. Лыкова НАН Беларуси}}, working under Teodor L. Perelman.<ref>G. E. Gorelik, "Stanislav Gennadyevich", in: ''Amazing Human Being'', p. 90.</ref> His research group focused on [[conformational analysis]] of [[peptides]]. In 1973, he defended his doctoral dissertation titled "Investigation of the Spatial Molecular Structure of Proteins and Peptides".<ref name=":1">{{Cite book |url=http://www.ximicat.com/ebook.php?file=volkensten_mbif.djv&page=96 |title=Molecular Biophysics |last=Volkenstein |first=M. V. |publisher=Nauka |year=1975 |pages=264 |language=ru |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120628115555/http://ximicat.com/ebook.php?file=volkensten_mbif.djv&page=96 |archive-date=28 June 2012}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Galaktionov |first=S. G. |date=1974 |title=Investigation of the Spatial Molecular Structure of Peptides and Proteins: Doctoral dissertation in biology / Institute of Heat and Mass Transfer, Academy of Sciences of the BSSR |url=https://e-catalog.nlb.by/Record/BY-NLB-br233572 |access-date=11 August 2025 |website=[[National Library of Belarus]] |publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences of Belarus]] |language=ru}}</ref><ref name="nan" />

In 1977, Galaktionov and his team moved to the {{ill|Latvian Institute of Organic Synthesis|lt=Latvian Institute of Organic Synthesis of the Academy of Sciences of the Latvian SSR|ru|Институт органического синтеза Академии наук Латвии}}, where he continued research on biologically active peptides. After returning to Minsk, he headed a laboratory at the {{ill|State Research Institute for Genetics and Selection of Industrial Microorganisms|lt=All-Union Research Institute for Genetics and Selection of Industrial Microorganisms|ru|ГосНИИгенетика}}, shifting focus to larger [[protein]] structures.<ref name="slovo" />

In 1991, he emigrated to the United States, joining the Center for Molecular Design at [[Washington University in St. Louis]] on the recommendation of Gregory V. Nikiforovich.<ref name="pavel115">Pavel G. Nikiforovich, "Saturdays in St. Louis", in: ''Amazing Human Being'', p. 115.</ref> He worked there for ten years under {{ill|Garland R. Marshall|de|Garland R. Marshall}}.<ref name="slovo" />

==Scientific work==
In the late 1960s, after joining the {{ill|A. V. Lykov Institute of Heat and Mass Transfer|lt=Institute of Heat and Mass Transfer of the Belarusian Academy of Sciences|ru|Институт тепло- и массообмена имени А. В. Лыкова НАН Беларуси}}, Galaktionov developed a [[mathematical algorithm]] for calculating the coordinates of any atom in a molecular chain based on the coordinates of preceding atoms. This innovation significantly reduced [[computation time]] and opened the prospect of [[Protein structure prediction|predicting the three-dimensional structures of proteins]]. Recognizing this as a central challenge in [[molecular biology]], Galaktionov formed a team of physicists and mathematicians, which soon produced calculations of [[amino acid]] structures and, by the mid-1970s, achieved a world first — a detailed [[computational model]] of the nine-amino-acid [[peptide]] [[bradykinin]]. The results were later confirmed experimentally and helped establish the understanding that linear peptides can spontaneously fold into structures resembling cyclic forms.{{sfn|Nikiforovich|2012|pp=445–446}}

Galaktionov's research focused on the [[molecular modelling]] of peptides and proteins, with applications in [[medicinal chemistry]] and [[drug design]]. He contributed to the development of computational approaches for studying peptide and [[Protein structure|protein conformations]], their [[structure–activity relationship]]s, and receptor interactions, including pioneering Soviet studies on the molecular mechanics of biologically active peptides and the conformational analysis of peptide hormones. His work also addressed the synthesis–structure–activity relationships of peptide and protein analogs, including modifications aimed at increasing their stability and activity, and the design of peptide drugs with improved pharmacological properties.{{sfn|Nikiforovich|2012|pp=445–447}}<ref name="NiT">{{Cite web |url=https://n-t.ru/ri/ga/ |title=Stanislav Galaktionov. Books. Science and Technology |website=Nauka i tekhnika |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706132517/http://www.n-t.ru/ri/ga/ |archive-date=6 July 2011 |language=en |url-status=live}}</ref>

At the same time, Galaktionov continued his research on the effects of ions on plants (the subject of his first dissertation), but now at a new — cellular — level. Together with {{ill|Vladimir Yurin (biologist)|lt=Vladimir Yurin|ru|Юрин, Владимир Михайлович}}, also a graduate of the [[Belarusian State Technological University|Forestry Institute]], he developed a theory describing the [[passive transport]] of ions through plant [[cell membrane]]s. Galaktionov pursued this work independently, without involving members of his "conformational" group, and co-authored two scientific monographs and three popular science books on the subject.{{sfn|Nikiforovich|2012|pp=445–447}}

Galaktionov developed a novel [[ab initio]] [[protein fold]] prediction method using contact-matrix constraints to exclude overly compact or extended folds, enabling efficient exploration of plausible structures for further modeling and refinement.{{sfn|Marshall|2004|p=13}}

He was the author of over 100 scientific works and several popular science books.<ref name="NiT" />{{sfn|Galaktionov|1988}} Galaktionov trained a number of students who went on to become Doctors and Candidates of Science, and founded a scientific school that continued its work around the world.{{sfn|Nikiforovich|2012|p=447}}<ref name="veresov">Valery G. Veresov, "S.G. Galaktionov and his role in my scientific destiny", in: ''Amazing Human Being'', pp. 54–62.</ref> His works were used in the curricula of higher education institutions in [[Russia]],<ref>{{Cite book |last=Sirotyuk |first=E. A. |url=https://mkgtu.ru/vikon/sveden/files/Metod_Biologicheskie_metody_kontrolya_kachestva_i_zaschity_biosfery.pdf |title=Biological Methods of Quality Control and Biosphere Protection: A Study Guide |publisher=Maikop State Technological University Press |year=2016 |edition=2nd |location=Maikop |page=63 |language=ru }}</ref> [[Belarus]]<ref>{{Cite book |last=Yurin |first=V. M. |url=https://elib.bsu.by/bitstream/123456789/104001/1/yurin2.pdf |title=Biomediators in Plants |publisher=[[Belarusian State University]] |year=2013 |isbn=978-985-518-902-3 |location=Minsk |page=198 |language=ru }}</ref> and [[Ukraine]]<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Omelyanchik |first1=L. O. |url=https://files.znu.edu.ua/files/Bibliobooks/Kolisnyk/0031050.pdf |title=Molecular mechanisms of hormonal and cytokine regulation |last2=Kolisnyk |first2=N. V. |publisher=[[Zaporizhzhia National University]] |year=2009 |location=Zaporizhzhia |language=uk }}</ref> through at least 2016.

== Scholarly reception ==
In Belarus, even as a candidate of sciences, Galaktionov's opinion was valued by leading Moscow professors.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://nashaniva.com/?c=ar&i=53547 |title=The Father of Molecular Modeling |last=Uskow |first=Yuras |date=20 April 2011 |website=[[Nasha Niva]] |publisher=Surodzichy Publishing |language=be |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813171349/https://nashaniva.com/?c=ar&i=53547 |archive-date=13 August 2022 |access-date=8 August 2025}}</ref> His research was highly regarded by leading Soviet scientists, including Academician [[Yuri Ovchinnikov (biochemist)|Yuri Ovchinnikov]], Professors {{ill|Oleg Ptitsyn|lt=Oleg Ptitsyn|ru|Птицын, Олег Борисович}} and {{ill|Alexander Kitaigorodsky|lt=Alexander Kitaigorodsky|ru|Китайгородский, Александр Исаакович}}.{{sfn|Nikiforovich|2012|p=446}}

Professor Gregory Nikiforovich described Galaktionov as one of the pioneers of [[molecular modelling]]<ref name="nan">Jubilee collection of the Institute of Experimental Botany, [[National Academy of Sciences of Belarus]], Minsk, 2011. Cited from ''Amazing Human Being'', St. Louis, 2011, pp. 8–11.</ref>{{sfn|Nikiforovich|2012|p=446}}<ref name="slovo">{{Cite web |last=Nikiforovich |first=G. V. |date=September 2011 |title=A Word About S. G. |url=http://7iskusstv.com/2011/Nomer9/Nikiforovich1.php |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120508170828/http://7iskusstv.com/2011/Nomer9/Nikiforovich1.php |archive-date=8 May 2012 |website=Seven Arts |volume=9 |language=ru |quote=abridged version |issue=22}}</ref> and praised his research on the passive transport of ions through plant cell membranes as successful.{{sfn|Nikiforovich|2012|pp=445–447}}

Recognizing the prospects of biophysics, as Professor Valery Veresov observed, Galaktionov initiated the creation of a corresponding scientific school in Belarus, which operated for many years at the world level and contributed to the development of related scientific fields.<ref name="veresov" />

Professor {{ill|Vladimir Yurin (biologist)|lt=Vladimir Yurin|ru|Юрин, Владимир Михайлович}} wrote that, in collective monographs, Galaktionov played a decisive role in interpreting the presented results. According to Yurin, in the 1970s Galaktionov was ahead of contemporary molecular biology in more than one area of research. Yurin also notes Galaktionov's skill in popularizing scientific ideas and explaining them to non-specialists.<ref name="yurin">Vladimir M. Yurin, "A friend for life", in: ''Amazing Human Being'', pp. 42–46.</ref>

According to Academician of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Belarus]] Professor {{ill|Viktor Parfenov|lt=Viktor Parfenov|ru|Парфёнов, Виктор Иванович}}, Galaktionov was among the researchers who enhanced the scientific prestige and recognition of the Belarusian {{ill|Institute of Experimental Botany|lt=Institute of Experimental Botany|ru|Институт экспериментальной ботаники имени В. Ф. Купревича НАН Беларуси}}.{{sfn|Parfenov|2011|p=21}}

Professor [[Harold Scheraga]] of [[Cornell University]] praised Galaktionov's studies on the structure of linear peptides, expressing regret that he could not become acquainted with them earlier because of the [[Iron Curtain]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Uskow |first=Yuras |date=20 April 2011 |title=The Father of Molecular Modeling |url=https://nashaniva.com/53547 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813171349/https://nashaniva.com/?c=ar&i=53547 |archive-date=13 August 2022 |access-date=8 August 2025 |website=[[Nasha Niva]] |publisher=Surodzichy Publishing |language=be}}</ref>{{sfn|Nikiforovich|2012|p=446}}

Professor {{ill|Garland R. Marshall|de|Garland R. Marshall}} highlighted Galaktionov as one of his long-term collaborators whose work had a significant impact on his scientific career.{{sfn|Marshall|2001|p=10}} Other scholars — including Tseitin, Veresov, Nikiforovich, and Yurin — acknowledged Galaktionov’s decisive role in their scientific careers and his support for their research.<ref name="veresov" /><ref name="yurin" />{{sfn|Tseitin|Nikiforovich|1999|p=311}}

Professor {{ill|Engels Doroshevich|lt=Engels Doroshevich|be|Энгельс Канстанцінавіч Дарашэвіч}} noted the large number of students who studied microbiology under Galaktionov and his talent as a lecturer.<ref name="Doroshevich">Engels K. Doroshevich, "Homo humanitatis et homo universalis — Stas Galaktionov", in: ''Amazing Human Being'', pp. 48–52.</ref>

==Views and habits==
Colleagues described Galaktionov as a meticulous and disciplined scientist, attentive to experimental detail and cautious in drawing conclusions.<ref name="slovo" /> He was known for a principled approach to publications, preferring to release only thoroughly verified results.<ref name="lora" /> According to contemporaries, his commitment to methodological rigor and accuracy was a defining feature of his research style.<ref name="marina" />

Galaktionov was skeptical about the [[Soviet system]]; he expressed his views in private conversations and, when possible, in professional settings.<ref name="slovo" /> He was also noted for supporting and protecting Jewish colleagues from [[Antisemitism in the USSR|workplace discrimination during the Soviet period]].<ref name="slovo" />
